entry.title: Research Summary: July 21, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is dominated by open multimodal foundation models and large-scale embodied AI. AV-Flamingo delivers fully open audio-visual reasoning over long videos from a top NVIDIA team. Xiaomi-Robotics-1 scales vision-language-action training to 100K+ hours of real-world trajectories, a major industry data effort.

  • Embodied AI and world models: Orbis 2 factorizes driving prediction into hierarchical coarse-to-fine diffusion; RynnBrain 1.1 ships cross-embodiment foundation models at 2B/9B/122B-A10B scales.
  • Safety and security: A rigorous n=4,100 human study finds AI voice phishing matches human scammers at far lower cost; Lucid compromises agent long-term memory via imperceptible image perturbations; honesty activation steering (StTP/StMP) restores misaligned model behavior.
  • Foundations: A unified theoretical-empirical framework attributes vector-quantization codebook collapse to distributional mismatch, relevant across tokenizers and generative models.

Ecosystem commentary is timely: Nathan Lambert analyzes Moonshot's 2.8T-parameter open-weights Kimi K3, while Jack Clark highlights UK AISI evidence that open-vs-closed cyber-capability gaps are narrowing.

entry.title: Audio-Visual Flamingo: Open Audio-Visual Intelligence for Long and Complex Videos

author.name: Sreyan Ghosh, Arushi Goel, Kaousheik Jayakumar, Lasha Koroshinadze, Nishit Anand, Siddharth Gururani, Hanrong Ye, Pritam Biswas, Yuanhang Su, Ehsan Hosseini-Asl, Sang-gil Lee, Zhifeng Kong, Jaehyeon Kim, Sungwon Kim, S Sakshi, Ramani Duraiswami, Dinesh Manocha, Andrew Tao, Mohammad Shoeybi, Bryan Catanzaro, Ming-Yu Liu, Wei Ping

entry.summary: AV-Flamingo is a fully open state-of-the-art audio-visual large language model for joint understanding and reasoning over audio, images, and long-form videos, supported by a ~7M-instance training collection and a three-stage curriculum from short-range perception to long-horizon reasoning. It targets long, complex real-world audio-visual videos.

entry.title: Orbis 2: A Hierarchical World Model for Driving

author.name: Sudhanshu Mittal, Arian Mousakhan, Silvio Galesso, Karim Farid, Jonannes Dienert, Rajat Sahay, Thomas Brox

entry.summary: Orbis 2 is a hierarchical world model for driving that factorizes future prediction into a high-level coarse-structure predictor over long horizons and a low-level detail generator, plus diffusion-forcing pretraining. It aims for both perceptual fidelity and spatial-semantic reasoning.

entry.title: AI Voice Phishing Performs on Par With Human Scammers at a Fraction of the Cost

author.name: Fred Heiding

entry.summary: A large human-subject study (n=4,100) measured susceptibility to AI-powered voice phishing across six leading voice models, finding compliance rates up to 36 percent and that participants could not reliably distinguish synthetic from human callers. An economic analysis suggests automated vishing is already profitable, highlighting a scalable and immediate misuse vector.

entry.title: EgoExoMoCap: Distributed Ego-Exo Human Motion Capture

author.name: Jiaxi Jiang, Bharat Lal Bhatnagar, Nan Yang, Lingni Ma, Sebastian Starke, Robin Kips, Nadine Bertsch, Christian Holz, Federica Bogo

entry.summary: EgoExoMoCap is a distributed framework that jointly leverages egocentric and exocentric multimodal signals from head-mounted devices for human motion estimation, unifying two paradigms usually studied separately. It avoids bulky multi-camera rigs or mocap suits.

entry.title: Searching Videos as Trees: Self-Correcting Agents for Grounded Long Video QA

author.name: Ce Zhang, Ziyang Wang, Yulu Pan, Oluwatumininu Oguntola, Pranav Wagh, Qiyu Wu, Hiromi Wakaki, Mohit Bansal, Gedas Bertasius

entry.summary: VideoTreeSearch casts grounded long-video question answering as iterative self-correcting search over an adaptive temporal tree built from visual scene boundaries, adding fine-to-coarse backtracking absent in prior single-crop agentic methods. This lets the agent recover from early mistakes.

entry.title: MLLM-DataEngine: Closing the Loop of Multimodal Instruction Tuning Data Generation

author.name: Zhiyuan Zhao, Bin Wang, Linke Ouyang, Yiqi Lin, Pan Zhang, Xiaoyi Dong, Jiaqi Wang, Conghui He

entry.summary: MLLM-DataEngine is a closed-loop system that analyzes model weaknesses from evaluation results, generates targeted incremental instruction-tuning data via adaptive bad-case sampling, and iteratively improves multimodal LLMs. It couples data generation, training, and benchmarking rather than treating them separately.

entry.title: RynnBrain 1.1: Towards More Capable and Generalizable Embodied Foundation Model

author.name: Kehan Li, Bohan Hou, Minghao Zhu, Tianyi Zhang, Zesen Cheng, Zhikai Wang, Sicong Leng, Xin Li, Xiao Lin, Biying Yao, Minghua Zeng, Jiangpin Liu, Ronghao Dang, Jiayan Guo, Siteng Huang, Haoyu Zhao, Heng Ping, Yaxi Zhao, Kexiang Wang, Tong Lu, Shengke Xue, Jiahao Tang, Yulei Wang, Zejing Wang, Jianwei Gao, Shijian Lu, Chengju Liu, Jianfei Yang, Mingxiu Chen, Deli Zhao

entry.summary: RynnBrain 1.1 is a family of embodied foundation models at 2B, 9B, and 122B-A10B scales trained with a unified spatio-temporal and physically grounded framework, adding contact-point prediction and native 3D grounding, plus a cross-embodiment VLA action model deployed on multiple humanoid platforms. It targets embodied perception, spatial reasoning, localization, and planning.

entry.title: An Exam for Active Observers

author.name: Jiarui Zhang, Muzi Tao, Shangshang Wang, Ollie Liu, Xuezhe Ma, Willie Neiswanger

entry.summary: ActiveVision is a benchmark of 17 tasks across 3 categories that measures whether multimodal LLMs perform active observation, forcing repeated visual perception rather than single static description. Frontier models including GPT-5.5 collapse on these tasks.

entry.title: Do Agents Dream of False Memories? Black-box Visual Attacks on Long-term Memory in Multimodal AI Agents

author.name: Halima Bouzidi, Mboutidem Ekemini Mkpong, Mohammad Abdullah Al Faruque

entry.summary: Lucid is a black-box adversarial framework that compromises multimodal AI agents' long-term memory pipelines using only imperceptible image perturbations, without access to the target MLLM, retrieval encoder, or text channel. It enables memory poisoning and other failure modes by exploiting unconditional trust in visual data.

entry.title: Rendering 3D Gaussians on a Graph Processor

author.name: Nicholas Fry, Ignacio Alzugaray, Mark Pupilli, Paul H. J. Kelly, Andrew J. Davison

entry.summary: This paper presents the first 3D Gaussian renderer on an Intelligence Processing Unit with only on-chip SRAM across 1,472 tiles, routing Gaussian primitives via Manhattan-distance hops on a NEWS grid under a bulk-synchronous-parallel model. It explores rendering on architectures approximating efficient sensor-processor designs.

entry.title: Distributional Matching for Vector Quantization: A Unified Theoretical and Empirical Framework

author.name: Xianghong Fang, Litao Guo, Hengchao Chen, Yuxuan Zhang, XiaofanXia, Dingjie Song, Yexin Liu, Hao Wang, Harry Yang, Qiang Sun, Yuan Yuan

entry.summary: This paper presents a unified theoretical and empirical framework attributing vector quantization instability and codebook collapse to a distribution mismatch between feature and code vectors, and proposes distributional matching to fix it. VQ underpins many visual representation and autoregressive models.

entry.title: Restoring Model Alignment via Honesty Activation Steering

author.name: niklas_herbster

entry.summary: The authors introduce two projection-aware activation-steering methods (StTP, StMP) that intervene only on tokens on the misaligned side of a learned boundary, restoring honesty while largely avoiding capability degradation. A single honesty direction generalizes across four out-of-distribution settings and persists through further finetuning, with sizable measured gains.

entry.title: PlanFlip: Attacking Multi-Agent LLM Systems via Planning-Phase Prompt Injection

author.name: Yuhang Wang

entry.summary: PlanFlip identifies the planning phase of multi-agent LLM systems as a high-leverage attack surface where a single prompt injection cascades across all downstream sub-tasks. It introduces four disguised injection attacks and evaluates nine frontier models, finding that stronger capability can amplify vulnerability.

entry.title: Research Summary: July 20, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is dominated by AI safety/alignment and embodied AI, with supporting advances in efficient serving and novel compute paradigms.

Safety and alignment occupy half the top ranks, reflecting a strong focus on reasoning-model vulnerabilities:

  • Open Distillation of Hereditary Traits (DeepMind) replicates that teacher traits transfer to students even after filtering related prompts and rollouts.
  • Hidden in Thought demonstrates transferable chain-of-thought artifacts that induce harmful behavior across many models.
  • Beyond a Single Direction shows chain-of-thought reinforces refusal, breaking simple single-direction activation steering.
  • Coercion and Deception introduces an agentic benchmark for unprompted escalation in AI-to-AI management hierarchies.
  • Many alignment techniques... unifies steering vectors, inoculation, and honesty fine-tuning as one train-one-deploy-another strategy.

Embodied AI leads overall: Xiaomi-Robotics-1 is a vision-language-action foundation model pretrained on 100K+ hours of real-world manipulation trajectories. Handroid contributes a reconfigurable 27-DoF body assemblable as either a dexterous hand or humanoid.

Efficiency and novel compute: PagedWeight runtime-quantizes MoE expert weights to balance precision against KV-cache growth, while a thermodynamic computing blueprint proposes energy-based hardware sampling via Langevin dynamics. VideoTreeSearch reframes grounded long-video QA as self-correcting search over adaptive temporal trees.

entry.title: Xiaomi-Robotics-1: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models with over 100K Hours of Real-World Trajectories

author.name: Xiaomi Robotics Team: Jun Guo, Piaopiao Jin, Jason Li, Peiyan Li, Yingyan Li, Futeng Liu, Wanli Peng, Optimus Qin, Yifei Su, Nan Sun, Qiao Sun, Runze Suo, Heyun Wang, Yunhong Wang, Rujie Wu, Caoyu Xia, Lina Zhang, Jack Zhao, Guoliang Chen, Wenlong Chen, Xinze He, Bin Li, Qing Li, Zhuorong Li, Heng Qu, Wenxuan Song, Diyun Xiang, Yifan Xie, Peiran Xu, Hangjun Ye, Wen Ye, Han Zhao, Quanyun Zhou

entry.summary: Xiaomi-Robotics-1 is a foundational vision-language-action model pretrained on over 100k hours of real-world manipulation trajectories collected via UMI devices, with a scalable auto-labeling pipeline describing scene transitions. It performs zero-shot mobile manipulation across unseen environments and adapts to new tasks with minimal fine-tuning.

entry.title: Open Distillation of Hereditary Traits

author.name: Arthur Conmy

entry.summary: Replicates and extends findings that distillation transfers a teacher model's traits to a base student even after filtering out prompts and rollouts that mention the trait, using accessible open-model setups instead of a frontier SFT pipeline. Demonstrations include transferring negative-emotion, agentic-misalignment, and censorship behaviors across several open models, with weights and code released.

entry.title: A Blueprint for Equilibrium-Based Differentiable Continuous-Variable Thermodynamic Computing

author.name: Owen Lockwood, J\'er\'emy B\'ejanin, Joost Bus, Christopher Chamberland, Patrick Huembeli, Frank Sch\"afer, Guillaume Verdon

entry.summary: Lays out a blueprint for energy-based thermodynamic computing hardware that samples from parameterized energy-based models via Langevin dynamics with tunable potentials, and shows how to train probabilistic graphical models natively on such hardware. It analyzes runtime and energy consumption as an alternative to conventional ML accelerators.

entry.title: Research Summary: July 19, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's set is dominated by AI safety, governance, and alignment discussion, largely sourced from LessWrong and the AI Alignment Forum, with little empirical or model-level research. Only 8 items were available, so all are ranked.

  • A Red Line and Oversight Framework for Government AI Contracts ranks highest: a first-hand mechanism-design proposal for constraining defense AI deployment, from a former Google DeepMind researcher, with direct policy relevance.
  • The Most Forbidden Technique is not always forbidden is the strongest technical item, synthesizing interpretability and RL to ask when model internals (probes) can safely serve as reward signals without inducing obfuscation.

Remaining items are conceptual or tangential:

  • Two Endogenous Alignment essays (a LessWrong original and an identical AI Alignment Forum cross-post) argue for internalized alignment via a child-rearing analogy, but are qualitative with no formal model; the duplicate adds no new content and is demoted.
  • Payorian FairBot revisits MIRI-style proof-based prisoner's-dilemma agents (niche but genuinely technical), while Map and Territory (rationality pedagogy), retina design, and a book review offer minimal original research value.

entry.title: Research Summary: July 18, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is dominated by AI safety, alignment, and control, led by concrete methodological and empirical contributions. Inoculation adapters (Center on Long-Term Risk) advance selective generalization by encoding an undesired trait in a LoRA during training rather than in prompts.

  • AI control: A LinuxArena study compares ten sandboxing protocols against an untrusted coding agent, yielding actionable deployment findings
  • Behavioral benchmarks: The TAC (Travel Agent Compassion) benchmark measures unprompted animal-welfare consideration in agents, reportedly adopted by a government safety institute
  • Evaluation critique: A methodological critique challenges labeling assumptions in Anthropic's agentic misalignment evaluations, arguing disobedience is mislabeled

Remaining alignment work includes a candid negative-result post-mortem on goal crystallisation and alignment-faking, a multi-agent LoRA finetuning experiment among frontier models (AI Village), and a structured alignment-technique taxonomy. Ecosystem and evaluation items round out the list: the new Corrigibility Research Fund ($200k+ in grants), a synthesis roundup, and a proposal to benchmark conceptual reasoning via expert judgment prediction.

Note: Two duplicate judgment-prediction items appeared (LessWrong original plus AI Alignment Forum crosspost); only the original is ranked. The provided initial scores were treated as advisory metadata, not directives.

entry.title: Research Summary: July 17, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's most significant work centers on safety/security and agentic methods. Pretraining data poisoning via computational propaganda (AI2/UW: Hajishirzi, Smith, Lo) demonstrates web-scale corpus contamination is feasible through public discussion interfaces, a high-impact security finding. The Refusal Residue probes alignment faking across a 13-model sweep, finding it emerges naturally in only two models, with asymmetric probe detectability.

  • T^2MLR fuses a cached middle-layer representation into an earlier layer for latent reasoning (Arora group)
  • Branching Policy Optimization exploits snapshottable agent sandboxes for prefix-sharing RL rollouts
  • Deconstructing Actor-Critic dissects RL design components across 33,000+ experiments for practitioners
  • A Schmidhuber-coauthored survey formalizes self-improvement in modern agentic systems

Foundation models and tooling extend to new domains:

  • Scaling Behavior Foundation Models studies scaling laws for humanoid whole-body control
  • scVision renders single cells as continuous images via optimal transport for single-cell biology
  • Generative Compilation delivers mid-decoding compiler feedback for typed-language code generation
  • A Rudin/Lakkaraju/Wong position paper argues explainability research must prioritize foundations over ad-hoc XAI methods

Note: The source contained only clean candidate listings and theme metadata; no embedded instructions or manipulation attempts were detected.

entry.title: Pretraining Data Can Be Poisoned through Computational Propaganda

author.name: Victoria Graf, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Noah A. Smith, David Kohlbrenner, Kyle Lo

entry.summary: This paper demonstrates that pretraining data poisoning is feasible at web scale by injecting content through public discussion interfaces, moving beyond prior Wikipedia-only settings, and introduces HalfLife to estimate whether adversarial content survives crawling and curation. It examines the interaction between poisoned data and real data-curation pipelines.

entry.title: T^2MLR: Transformer with Temporal Middle-Layer Recurrence

author.name: Ziyang Cai, Xingyu Zhu, Yihe Dong, Yinghui He, Sanjeev Arora

entry.summary: T2MLR is a latent-reasoning Transformer variant that fuses a cached middle-layer representation from the previous token into an earlier layer of the current token, letting abstract intermediate computation persist across decoding steps with little overhead. It reports consistent gains over matched Transformer baselines on pretraining and multi-hop reasoning.

entry.title: Scaling Behavior Foundation Model for Humanoid Robots

author.name: Weishuai Zeng, Kangning Yin, Xiaojie Niu, Shunlin Lu, Weixiang Zhong, Jiahe Chen, Feiyu Jia, Xiao Chen, Zirui Wang, Furui Xu, Ming Zhou, Kailin Li, Weinan Zhang, He Wang, Li Yi, Dahua Lin, Jiangmiao Pang, Jingbo Wang

entry.summary: Revisits the scaling recipe for Behavior Foundation Models for humanoid whole-body control, studying how learning paradigm, behavioral data, and model architecture should be coordinated for effective scaling. It targets expressive, versatile, generalizable humanoid control as a foundation for generalist embodied agents.

entry.title: The Refusal Residue: When Probes Catch Alignment Faking and When They Don't

author.name: Aman Mehta

entry.summary: Studies alignment faking across a 13-model sweep, finding natural faking emerges only in two models and probing their hidden states reveals an asymmetric refusal residue distinguishing strategic from genuine compliance. It examines whether internal representations expose deception that outputs conceal.

entry.title: Branching Policy Optimization: Sandbox-Native Language Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Bowei He, Yankai Chen, Xiaokun Zhang, Xue Liu

entry.summary: Proposes Branching Policy Optimization, which exploits the deterministic and snapshottable nature of agent sandboxes to build a single prefix-sharing rollout tree rather than N independent trajectories. This rethinks the rollout topology inherited from RLHF for LLM agent training.

entry.title: Research Summary: July 16, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research spans decentralized training, agentic reinforcement learning, and AI-human interaction safety. Agora proposes permissionless, internet-scale LLM pretraining across heterogeneous, individually-owned GPUs, directly challenging datacenter concentration of frontier training.

  • RL post-training leads: TRACE assigns dense turn-level credit for long-horizon agents; GFlowRL scales distribution-matching RL by removing the learned prompt-conditional partition function; one study maps optimal FLOP allocation across policy size, search, and feedback
  • Safety and alignment: a preregistered study (5 experiments, 3,000+ participants) shows AI advice nearly eliminates willingness to say 'I don't know', even when wrong; chain-of-thought stays monitorable when unfaithfulness requires computation
  • Multimodal and systems: SC-CMJP couples image-text generation within masked diffusion for cross-modal self-correction; Meta FAIR's Cluster with Auctions jointly learns balanced partitions for vector search; on-policy distillation is reframed as an exploration catalyst, alongside a survey formalizing self-improving agentic systems.

Note: entry [eda7c336089c] shows a title/summary mismatch (superposition vs. NL-autoencoder monitoring) and was treated as a data-quality flag, not ranked.

entry.title: Agora: Collective and Permissionless Internet-Scale Pretraining of Large Language Models

author.name: Gil Avraham, Violetta Shevchenko, Hadi Mohaghegh Dolatabadi, Karol Pajak, James Snewin, Harry Xi, Rodney O'Donnell, Thalaiyasingam Ajanthan, Sameera Ramasinghe, Chamin Hewa Koneputugodage, Shamane Siriwardhana, Alexander Long

entry.summary: Agora is a system for permissionless, internet-scale pretraining of large language models across heterogeneous, preemptible, individually owned GPUs, combining bandwidth-efficient pipeline-parallel sharding with fault-tolerant multi-party coordination. It aims to unlock consumer and prosumer compute currently unusable for frontier training.

entry.title: TRACE: Turn-level Reward Assignment via Credit Estimation for Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: Leitian Tao, Baolin Peng, Wenlin Yao, Tao Ge, Hao Cheng, Mike Hang Wang, Jianfeng Gao, Sharon Li

entry.summary: TRACE assigns dense turn-level rewards to long-horizon agentic RL by estimating per-step credit from state transitions, addressing the sparsity and high variance of outcome-only rewards over tens or hundreds of tool calls. It aims to correctly credit useful intermediate actions in failed rollouts.

entry.title: AI advice suppresses people's willingness to say "I don't know", even when the advice is wrong and accuracy is incentivized

author.name: Chiara Marcoccia, Walter Quattrociocchi, Valerio Capraro

entry.summary: In five experiments with over 3,000 participants, access to AI advice nearly eliminated people's willingness to say I do not know, even when the advice was engineered to be wrong and accuracy was incentivized. Participants answered more but were correct about a third as often while confidence roughly doubled.

entry.title: Concurrent Image Understanding and Generation: Self-Correcting Coupled Markov Jump Processes

author.name: Minh-Quan Le, Armand Comas, Alexandros Lattas, Stylianos Moschoglou, Pedro V\'elez, Amit Raj, Aaron Germuth, Thabo Beeler, Dimitris Samaras, Di Qiu

entry.summary: SC-CMJP couples image and text generation within masked diffusion models so that one modality can correct the other in the same decoding step, addressing the inability of standard samplers to detect and repair cross-modal contradictions. The framework enables a self-correcting joint understanding-generation loop.

entry.title: GFlowRL: Scaling Distribution-Matching RL to Large Language Models

author.name: Xiaodong Liu, Michael Xu, Jack W. Stokes, Paul Smolensky, Doug Burger, Jianfeng Gao

entry.summary: GFlowRL scales GFlowNet-style distribution-matching RL to large reasoning models by removing the learned prompt-conditional partition function that causes gradient instability at scale, replacing it with a simpler alternative. It aims to preserve diverse reasoning paths without collapsing to dominant modes in modern post-training pipelines.

entry.title: Self-Improvements in Modern Agentic Systems: A Survey

author.name: Zhe Ren, Yimeng Chen, Dandan Guo, Guowei Rong, Tonghui Li, R. B. Xiong, Qingfeng Lan, Wenyi Wang, Li Nanbo, Yibo Yang, Mingchen Zhuge, J\"urgen Schmidhuber

entry.summary: A survey framing modern self-improving agents as adaptive systems that turn experience into accumulated capability, formalizing self-improvement as a self-induced update operator over model parameters or scaffold components. It organizes prior work by update target and driving signal.

entry.title: LLM CoTs remain monitorable when being unfaithful requires computation

author.name: arav-dhoot

entry.summary: This replication and extension of prior work finds that chain-of-thought unfaithfulness in language models mostly happens on easy tasks, while hints requiring actual computation are verbalized near baseline, keeping reasoning monitorable. Tested across eleven models from six families, it also separates cue-susceptibility from concealment and argues safety cases must be per-model rather than universal.

entry.title: Research Summary: July 15, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research spans frontier-scale RL, mechanistic interpretability, and foundational theory. Ring-Zero scales zero-RL with verifiable rewards to a trillion-parameter model, probing emergent reasoning at unprecedented scale.

  • Interpretability & theory: A reusable countdown subcircuit is shared across tasks in Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct (Gurnee, Ameisen); Thompson Sampling is proven 2-competitive for mistakes, resolving a long-standing conjecture (Sellke, Valiant).
  • Memorization & reliability: Extractable memorization is reframed from first principles (Liang, Lemley, Ho, Cooper), requiring matched generation-probability comparisons; DeepMind grounds LLM confidence in normative statistical decision theory.
  • Safety & alignment: 'Distributed Denial of Science' models indirect data poisoning as industrialized scientific fraud; unsupervised failure attribution traces agent errors from successful trajectories (S. Li).
  • Embodied & vision: Xiaomi-Robotics-U0 (38B) unifies embodied generation as a world foundation model; RINO casts diverse vision signals as RGB-to-RGB; function-aware fill-in-the-middle mid-training targets coding-agent foundation models.
entry.content:
Today's research spans frontier-scale RL, mechanistic interpretability, and foundational theory. Ring-Zero scales zero-RL with verifiable rewards to a trillion-parameter model, probing emergent reasoning at unprecedented scale.

  • Interpretability & theory: A reusable countdown subcircuit is shared across tasks in Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct (Gurnee, Ameisen); Thompson Sampling is proven 2-competitive for mistakes, resolving a long-standing conjecture (Sellke, Valiant).
  • Memorization & reliability: Extractable memorization is reframed from first principles (Liang, Lemley, Ho, Cooper), requiring matched generation-probability comparisons; DeepMind grounds LLM confidence in normative statistical decision theory.
  • Safety & alignment: 'Distributed Denial of Science' models indirect data poisoning as industrialized scientific fraud; unsupervised failure attribution traces agent errors from successful trajectories (S. Li).
  • Embodied & vision: Xiaomi-Robotics-U0 (38B) unifies embodied generation as a world foundation model; RINO casts diverse vision signals as RGB-to-RGB; function-aware fill-in-the-middle mid-training targets coding-agent foundation models.

entry.title: Ring-Zero: Scaling Zero RL to a Trillion Parameters for Emergent Reasoning

author.name: Xinyu Tang, Gangqiang Cao, Yurou Liu, Yuliang Zhan, Xiaochong Lan, Yifan Li, Yuchen Yan, Han Peng, Zican Dong, Zhenduo Zhang, Tianshu Wang, Xinyu Kong, Zujie Wen, Wayne Xin Zhao, Zhiqiang Zhang, Jun Zhou

entry.summary: Ring-Zero scales zero reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards to a trillion-parameter model to study large-scale training dynamics and emergent reasoning, addressing naive scaling problems like poor readability, token redundancy, and inflexible reasoning depth. It introduces a stable, efficient pipeline with algorithmic and systems optimizations including clipping strategies. It pushes zero-RL reasoning to an unprecedented scale.

entry.title: A Shared Subcircuit Lets LLMs Count Down Across Tasks

author.name: Jacob Dunefsky, Wes Gurnee, Emmanuel Ameisen

entry.summary: This mechanistic-interpretability study identifies a reusable countdown subcircuit inside Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct that tracks how many tokens remain before a target length across tasks like fixed-length sentences, DNA codon endings, and ASCII tables. The authors characterize the geometric representation the circuit uses to estimate remaining positions. It matters as evidence that models reuse general-purpose internal machinery across superficially different tasks.

entry.title: Thompson Sampling Is 2-Competitive for Mistakes

author.name: Mark Sellke, Gregory Valiant

entry.summary: This theory paper proves Thompson sampling incurs at most twice the expected number of suboptimal-arm selections of any policy for Bayesian bandits with independent, rest-only-evolving arms. This confirms a 2014 conjecture of Guha and Munagala with a tight factor of two. It provides a clean competitive-ratio guarantee for a widely used algorithm.

entry.title: Function-Aware Fill-in-the-Middle as Mid-Training for Coding Agent Foundation Models

author.name: Yubo Wang, Jiarong Liang, Yuxuan Zhang, Xuye Liu, Cong Wei, Yuyu Zhang, Ping Nie, Wenhu Chen

entry.summary: This paper proposes function-aware fill-in-the-middle mid-training for coding agents, arguing that an agent action-observation-continuation loop is structurally the same as a function call site available at internet scale in ordinary code. It masks functions selected by program dependency graph analysis under a complexity-inferability criterion and mid-trains an open coding model to better integrate tool returns into reasoning.

entry.title: Distributed Denial of Science: How Indirect Data Poisoning of AI Systems Can Industrialize Scientific Fraud

author.name: B\'alint Gyevn\'ar, Atoosa Kasirzadeh, Nihar B. Shah

entry.summary: Introduces and empirically evaluates indirect data poisoning as a threat to scientific integrity, where adversaries corrupt public datasets that autonomous research agents unknowingly ingest and propagate. It argues AI-automated science could industrialize scientific fraud at scale.

entry.title: Xiaomi-Robotics-U0: Unified Embodied Synthesis with World Foundation Model

author.name: Xinghang Li, Jun Guo, Qiwei Li, Long Qian, Hang Lai, Yueze Wang, Hongyu Yan, Jiahang Cao, Xi Chen, Jingen Qu, Jiaxi Song, Nan Sun, Hanye Zhao, Futeng Liu, Wanli Peng, Heyun Wang, Yunhong Wang, Caoyu Xia, Jack Zhao, Diyun Xiang, Hangjun Ye, Heng Qu, Huaping Liu, Jason Li

entry.summary: Xiaomi-Robotics-U0 is a 38-billion-parameter multimodal autoregressive model that treats embodied generation as an extension of foundation image and video generation, jointly optimizing text-to-image, editing, embodied scene generation, embodied transfer, and embodied video generation. It matters as a large industry effort to build a unified world foundation model for robotics.

entry.title: Tracing Agentic Failure from the Flow of Success

author.name: Samuel Yeh, Yiwen Zhu, Shaleen Deep, Sharon Li

entry.summary: The paper addresses unsupervised failure attribution for LLM agent systems, training only on successful trajectories to identify which step caused a failure at inference time. This avoids expensive step-level error annotations and prompting pipelines, making debugging of agentic systems more scalable.

entry.title: Extractable Memorization From First Principles

author.name: A. Feder Cooper, Marika Swanberg, Jamie Hayes, Lea Duesterwald, Christopher De Sa, Daniel E. Ho, Mark A. Lemley, Percy Liang

entry.summary: This paper reframes extractable memorization in LLMs from first principles, arguing valid extraction claims require matched comparison of generation probabilities between training and comparable non-training sequences to distinguish memorization from mere predictability. Authors include prominent researchers spanning ML, law, and policy. It clarifies methodology in a contested legally relevant area.

entry.title: Language Identification with Succinct Machine-Independent Traces

author.name: Moses Charikar, Jon Kleinberg, Chirag Pabbaraju

entry.summary: Motivated by LLMs, this paper studies Gold-Angluin language identification when learners are given succinct machine-independent computational traces or annotations, akin to commented code or chain-of-thought. It proves positive identifiability results that circumvent classic negative results. It offers a theoretical lens on why annotated training data helps learning.

entry.title: Scaling Point-in-Time Language Models

author.name: Bryan Kelly, Semyon Malamud, Johannes Schwab, Teng Andrea Xu

entry.summary: This work builds point-in-time language models trained only on text available up to each calendar date to eliminate lookahead bias that invalidates financial and social-science backtests. Scaling decoder-only transformers to 4B parameters on 1T chronologically filtered FineWeb tokens narrows the performance gap to unconstrained models, with monthly checkpoints. It matters for causally valid empirical research.

entry.title: A Learning-Rate-Gated Failure of GRPO in a Small Language and Vision-Language Model Web Agent: A Controlled Null and Its Mechanism

author.name: Chengguang Gan, Zhixi Cai, Yunhao Liang, Hanjun Wei, Shiwen Ni, Qinghao Zhang

entry.summary: A carefully controlled study finds that GRPO reinforcement learning fails to add skill to small (4-8B) language and vision-language web agents beyond a strong supervised baseline, and can make text agents worse at high learning rates. It analyzes the mechanism as learning-rate-gated reshaping rather than genuine capability gain.

entry.title: Research Summary: July 14, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research centers on foundational advances in scaling laws, sequence architectures, and training efficiency, complemented by high-impact safety and formal-verification work.

Architecture & efficiency:

  • DSSMs augment diagonal state-space recurrences with delayed-state feedback from delay differential equations, addressing fixed-state compression limits.
  • Requential Coding (Wilson, Finzi) reframes model compression via teacher-selected self-generated training data.
  • M+Adam hybridizes additive and multiplicative updates to stabilize low-precision training.
  • Sticky Jump Diffusions unify masked, continuous, and hybrid diffusion in one simulation-free framework.

Scaling, evaluation & world models:

  • Domain-Aware Scaling Laws formalize and quantify cross-domain data synergy in pretraining mixtures.
  • AdvancedMathBench offers 296 process-aware problems for proof generation and verification.
  • A control theory of predictability argues held-out prediction error is an unreliable latent world-model objective.

Safety, security & agents:

  • MIT/Thorn introduce non-generative auditing to detect whether open models can produce illegal CSAM content.
  • Microsoft Research scales formal verification of production SymCrypt Rust cryptography using the Aeneas tool.
  • ScaleCUA scales computer-use agents through verifiable task synthesis (VeriGen) and efficient online RL.

entry.title: DSSMs: State Space Models with Explicit Memory via Delay Differential Equations

author.name: Yixiao Qian, Song Chen, Jiaxu Liu, Shengze Cai, Chao Xu

entry.summary: Proposes Delay State Space Models that augment diagonal SSM recurrences with explicit delayed-state feedback inspired by delay differential equations, adding stability parameterization and FFT-based training tools. The goal is to improve long-range retrieval in efficient linear-time sequence models.

entry.title: Domain-Aware Scaling Laws Uncover Data Synergy

author.name: Kimia Hamidieh, Lester Mackey, David Alvarez-Melis

entry.summary: Formalizes and quantifies data synergy in LLM pretraining, where combining domains yields more or less than the sum of parts, using domain-aware scaling laws estimated from observational variation across open-weight models. It captures effects like code improving math reasoning versus interference between mixtures.

entry.title: AdvancedMathBench: A Benchmark Suite for Advanced Mathematical Proof Generation and Verification

author.name: Lingkai Kong, Zijian Wu, Yuzhe Gu, Haiteng Zhao, Wenyong Huang, Shuang Sun, Zhicheng Xiong, Xiaotian Zhang, Shuya Zhao, Yan Wang, Disheng Xu, Wenwei Zhang, Kai Chen

entry.summary: Introduces AdvancedMathBench and its ProverBench component, a suite of 296 undergraduate-to-doctoral-level problems for evaluating advanced mathematical proof generation and verification with process-level rather than final-answer judgments. It aims to expose the poorly understood limits of LLM reasoning beyond olympiad math.

entry.title: Verifying Rust cryptography in SymCrypt, from standards to code

author.name: Son Ho, Cédric Fournet, Antoine Delignat-Lavaud, Samuel Lee, Jason Fisher, Jessica Krynitsky

entry.summary: Microsoft Research describes scaling formal verification of production cryptography by proving Rust implementations correct using the Aeneas tool and Lean, with AI agents writing independently-verifiable proofs. They release verified code, specs, and proofs for SHA-3 and post-quantum ML-KEM.

entry.title: Requential Coding: Pushing the Limits of Model Compression with Self-Generated Training Data

author.name: Shikai Qiu, Marc Finzi, Yujia Zheng, Kun Zhang, Andrew Gordon Wilson

entry.summary: Proposes requential coding, a compression scheme where a teacher model selects training data so codes reflect learned information rather than model size or raw data entropy. It reframes model compression through the lens of intelligence as compression.

entry.title: Empowering Long-form Omni-modal Understanding with Robust Audio Perception

author.name: Kaiying Yan, Luoyi Sun, Xiao Zhou, Weidi Xie

entry.summary: Introduces AVDC, a large-scale dataset with decoupled visual-only, audio-only, and joint audio-visual captions produced by an automated pipeline, to advance long-form omni-modal understanding with robust audio perception. It targets the under-explored role of explicitly aligned auditory cues in multimodal models.

entry.title: A Control Theory of Predictability in Latent World Models

author.name: Hanzhe You, Yonggang Zhang, Maohao Ran, Zhiqin Yang, Zhenyuan Zhang, Wei Xue, Jun Song, Xinmei Tian, Yike Guo

entry.summary: Argues that prediction error on held-out data is an unreliable objective for latent world models because planners query the model off the data manifold, and reframes the objective around control-relevant discrepancy. This challenges standard model-selection practice in model-based planning.

entry.title: M+Adam: Low-Precision Training via Additive-Multiplicative Optimization

author.name: Xiaoyuan Liang, Sebastian Loeschcke, Mads Toftrup, Anima Anandkumar

entry.summary: Proposes M+Adam, which combines additive and multiplicative optimizer updates to overcome complementary failure modes in low-precision training, where additive updates stall at large magnitudes and multiplicative ones fail near zero and sign changes. It targets accurate training with quantized weights.

entry.title: Sticky Jump Diffusions: A Unifying View of Masked, Continuous, and Hybrid Diffusion

author.name: Pascal Jutras-Dub\'e, Patrick Pynadath, Jeremy Lu, Yuan Gao, Ruqi Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces Sticky Jump Diffusions, continuous-time processes whose discrete anchors are token embeddings, unifying masked, continuous, and hybrid diffusion as limiting cases with a denoising-hazard-matching training objective. It provides a common theoretical lens for diverse discrete-and-continuous diffusion models.

entry.title: UniPose9D: Universal Category-Agnostic Object Pose Estimation

author.name: Yang You, Yi Du, Cole Harrison, Leonidas Guibas

entry.summary: Introduces UniPose9D, a category-agnostic foundation model for 9D object pose estimation that predicts rotation, translation, and metric size from RGB-D or RGB-with-depth inputs without category labels, CAD models, or reference views. It combines DINOv2 and PointNet features over sampled point pairs to predict NOCS coordinates.

entry.title: New method aims to keep kids safe from illegal AI-generated content

author.name: Adam Zewe | MIT News

entry.summary: MIT researchers with Thorn developed an auditing method that determines whether an open-source generative model can produce child sexual abuse material without ever prompting it to generate such content, sidestepping the legal impossibility of direct testing. It responds to the sharp rise in reported AI-generated CSAM.
